predictedRisks.riskTitle: Sprint 5 and PAT Delay from Unresolved High-Severity Dependencies
predictedRisks.riskDescription: Open high-severity client and joint-team dependencies may delay Sprint 5 completion and cascade into PAT, code freeze, regression, and go-live. The project is already behind the contractual phase baseline, leaving minimal recovery capacity.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Critical dependency resolution is lagging late in build, including chat-based escalation clarification, Azure monitoring process confirmation, automation environment provisioning, and Guru Card fit assessment.
triggerConditions: Any high-severity dependency remains unresolved beyond Sprint 5 start
Automation testing environment is not fully provisioned for planned validation activities
Escalation workflow requirements remain ambiguous during Sprint 5 build
Azure monitoring and failure-alert process remains pending at PAT entry

potentialImpact.schedule: Sprint 5 completion slips, pushing PAT start and compressing regression and deployment windows
potentialImpact.cost: Extended resource usage and possible hidden overrun pressure under fixed-price delivery
potentialImpact.quality: Late dependency resolution may force incomplete testing or workaround-based implementation
potentialImpact.customer: Reduced stakeholder confidence and delayed business validation
potentialImpact.operations: Go-live readiness activities and support preparation may be deferred

supportingPatterns: Historical Sprint 1 slip driven by broader scope and client cloud/environment dependencies
Current WSR still shows unresolved environment and integration dependencies at Week 11
Historical pattern shows early dependency issues cascading into later schedule erosion

mitigationPlan: Escalate all open high-severity dependencies to steering-level owners with dated resolution commitments
Create a daily dependency burn-down with named client and vendor owners
Sequence Sprint 5 work to isolate blocked vs unblocked features
Pre-stage PAT planning and test data readiness in parallel where dependencies allow
recommendations: Impose a hard dependency closure checkpoint before Sprint 5 critical path execution
Establish fallback options for non-critical integration items to protect PAT start
Track dependency age, owner responsiveness, and impact-to-milestone weekly and daily until stabilized
predictedRisks.reasoning: The project is 2-3 weeks behind contractual phase expectations, has no meaningful downstream float, and still carries four high-severity dependencies at 68.75% elapsed time. Historical evidence from the same delivery family shows dependency-driven slippage recurring and propagating forward.
monitoringIndicators: Dependency closure dates vs committed dates

projectIndicators: 4 high-severity dependencies in progress at Week 11
Schedule health marked UNDER REVIEW
Sequential critical path with no slack: Sprint 5 -> PAT -> Code Freeze -> Regression -> Deployment
Actual phase still Build & Test while contractual phase should be UAT Sign Off

predictedRisks.riskTitle: PAT Rework Surge Delays Code Freeze and Regression Start
predictedRisks.riskDescription: Recurring defects and enhancement feedback from early PAT reviews may continue into formal PAT, causing a higher-than-planned rework load that delays code freeze and compresses regression.
predictedRisks.rootCause: Persistent quality issues across multiple sprints, ongoing enhancement intake, and incomplete front-end test coverage are creating rework cycles rather than converging toward stable release readiness.
triggerConditions: PAT identifies additional critical or high-priority defects
Enhancement requests continue to enter the sprint backlog during final build stages
Front-end/UI defects remain a disproportionate share of open items
Definition-of-done remains insufficient for release-critical paths

potentialImpact.schedule: Code freeze slips beyond Sept 18 and regression start is delayed
potentialImpact.cost: Additional triage, retest, and defect-resolution effort consumes unplanned team capacity
potentialImpact.quality: Defect leakage risk rises if regression is shortened to preserve go-live
potentialImpact.customer: Business users may lose confidence due to repeated validation findings
potentialImpact.operations: Training, deployment rehearsal, and readiness activities may be disrupted

supportingPatterns: Historical pattern of feedback-driven rework affecting validation and implementation
Expanded PAT/regression scope historically emerged after project initiation
Current project shows PAT feedback from prior sprints already being prioritized into current sprint

mitigationPlan: Enforce defect triage thresholds separating true defects from deferred enhancements
Set release-quality gates for critical user journeys before PAT entry
Prioritize front-end/UI automation for highest-risk validation rules and workflows
Prepare rapid decision forum for scope containment during PAT
recommendations: Freeze non-essential enhancements before formal PAT begins
Publish severity-based exit criteria for PAT and code freeze
Run targeted dry-run validation of integrated workflow prior to PAT kickoff
predictedRisks.reasoning: Evidence shows recurring quality issues across Sprints 1-4, PAT early verification findings already causing rework, and significant UI-related bugs. With formal PAT and regression still ahead, unresolved quality debt is likely to surface in the next phase rather than disappear.

projectIndicators: PAT early verification testing generated defects and enhancement requests
Recurring quality issues observed across multiple sprints
Bug list notes significant UI-related bugs and enhancements
Quality status is UNDER REVIEW

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Compressed Testing Window Causes Incomplete Regression and Go-Live Readiness Risk
predictedRisks.riskDescription: Because development is already behind the original lifecycle baseline, the planned PAT and regression windows may become compressed further, increasing the likelihood of incomplete validation before deployment.
predictedRisks.rootCause: The project has significant downstream sequential testing activities with no schedule buffer, while development and rework are still consuming time that should have been allocated to UAT/PAT readiness.
triggerConditions: Sprint 5 finishes late or with carryover defects
PAT completion moves beyond planned end date
Regression is shortened to preserve October deployment target
Test environment instability or incomplete automation slows execution

potentialImpact.schedule: Deployment window slips or becomes highly compressed
potentialImpact.cost: Postponement or intensified hypercare raises support effort
potentialImpact.quality: Critical end-to-end, integration, or edge-case defects may escape into production
potentialImpact.customer: User confidence and acceptance may weaken if defects appear post-deployment
potentialImpact.operations: Increased hypercare incident volume and unstable transition to steady-state support

supportingPatterns: Historical PAT and regression expansion beyond SOW baseline
Historical sprint slip reduced validation window and contributed to downstream compression
Enterprise pattern shows dependency delays -> reduced validation window -> rework -> expanded testing -> schedule drift

mitigationPlan: Pre-stage regression suite completion and environment readiness before code freeze
Protect minimum test coverage thresholds for critical business flows
Use go/no-go phase gates with executive escalation if exit criteria are not met
Prepare phased or controlled deployment contingency if full-scope readiness is not achieved
recommendations: Do not trade critical regression depth for date adherence without executive risk acceptance
Track daily burn against PAT and regression scope completion
Prioritize integrated workflow, escalation, access control, and production-monitoring scenarios
predictedRisks.reasoning: The current plan contains PAT, code freeze, regression, deployment, training, and hypercare in tight sequence. With the project already behind the contractual baseline and quality issues still being resolved, testing compression is a highly probable forward risk.
monitoringIndicators: Environment uptime and test execution throughput

projectIndicators: Testing phase compression explicitly identified in current delivery intelligence
Project already moved from 16-week baseline to 22-week projected duration
PAT and regression are sequential with no slack
Actual project phase is behind contractual lifecycle

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Client Review and PAT Responsiveness Delays Acceptance and Final Sign-Off
predictedRisks.riskDescription: Upcoming demo, PAT, and acceptance activities require timely client feedback and SME participation. Delayed reviews or incomplete tester availability may delay acceptance decisions and extend implementation cycles.
predictedRisks.rootCause: The delivery model depends heavily on client review cycles, while historical evidence shows feedback timing risk and the current program continues to incorporate review-driven fixes into active sprints.
triggerConditions: Client feedback is not returned within the expected review window
PAT testers or SMEs are unavailable for scheduled validation sessions
Business decisions on defects vs enhancements are delayed
Integrated workflow demo yields unresolved business clarification items

potentialImpact.schedule: PAT completion and business sign-off are delayed
potentialImpact.cost: Extended validation cycles consume additional team coordination and support effort
potentialImpact.quality: Late business clarification can force rushed fixes or deferrals
potentialImpact.customer: Stakeholder frustration may increase due to repeated review loops
potentialImpact.operations: Deployment readiness and training preparation may be postponed

supportingPatterns: Historical customer feedback timing risk directly affected sprint validation and implementation
Current PAT-driven rework pattern shows review responsiveness remains structurally important
SOW acceptance criteria assumes rapid client review, increasing sensitivity to response delays

mitigationPlan: Lock PAT calendar, named testers, and business approvers before PAT start
Define response-time SLAs and escalation thresholds for review items
Separate approval decisions from enhancement backlog discussions
Provide test scripts and expected outcomes in advance to reduce decision latency
recommendations: Pre-book daily defect triage and twice-weekly business decision sessions during PAT
Obtain backup SME coverage for critical review windows
Use acceptance dashboards showing open blockers, due dates, and pending owner decisions
predictedRisks.reasoning: The project is entering a review-intensive stage, and historical evidence from the same client context shows feedback timing can affect validation and implementation. Current evidence confirms PAT feedback loops are already influencing sprint content and schedule pressure.

projectIndicators: SOW requires client review within 3 business days
PAT planned for 15 days with heavy client involvement
Current sprint is already absorbing PAT feedback and fixes
Client dependencies remain active late in the program

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Late-Stage GPT-5 Mini Migration Causes Functional Regression or Validation Delay
predictedRisks.riskDescription: The planned migration to GPT-5 Mini during Sprint 5 may introduce behavioral, integration, or performance changes late in the delivery lifecycle, increasing the risk of regression and additional validation effort before PAT and go-live.
predictedRisks.rootCause: A technology change is being introduced in the final build sprint of an already schedule-constrained AI-enabled solution with multiple integrated components and active quality concerns.
triggerConditions: Model migration changes output quality, latency, or business-rule behavior
Validation metrics do not match pre-migration baseline
Prompt, workflow, or integration behavior requires retuning after migration
Migration defects are discovered during PAT instead of pre-PAT validation

potentialImpact.schedule: Additional validation and tuning delay Sprint 5 closure or PAT readiness
potentialImpact.cost: Extra testing and remediation effort is required
potentialImpact.quality: LLM output drift, edge-case failures, or inconsistent escalation behavior may occur
potentialImpact.customer: Confidence in AI outcomes may be reduced if behavior changes are visible to users
potentialImpact.operations: Production support burden increases if migration-related issues escape to go-live

supportingPatterns: No direct historical analog in supplied risk history
However, historical pattern shows late changes and expanded validation activities tend to increase schedule and testing pressure
Current project has high technical and integration complexity with limited schedule slack

mitigationPlan: Baseline current model behavior before migration using agreed validation metrics
Run migration in non-production with rollback criteria and explicit acceptance thresholds
Limit concurrent functional changes during migration window
Defer migration if benefit does not outweigh schedule and validation risk
recommendations: Treat model migration as a gated technical change, not a routine sprint task
Require pre- and post-migration benchmark sign-off
Prepare rollback-to-prior-model option until PAT stability is confirmed
predictedRisks.reasoning: The migration is explicitly planned for Sprint 5, which is on the critical path before PAT. Because the project is already under schedule and quality pressure, even a moderate technical issue could have disproportionate downstream effect.
monitoringIndicators: Pre/post migration accuracy and latency metrics

projectIndicators: Sprint 5 plan includes migration to GPT-5 Mini and post-transition validation
LLM selection and evaluation are still in progress
Technical and integration complexity assessed as HIGH
No schedule buffer available for major late-stage technical rework

predictedRisks.riskTitle: Formal Change-Control and Milestone Re-Baselining Failure Escalates into Acceptance or Payment Dispute
predictedRisks.riskDescription: If the current inferred extension and revised testing/deployment sequence remain operationally active without formal contractual re-baselining, the project may face milestone acceptance ambiguity, payment timing disputes, and heightened governance friction before go-live and hypercare completion.
predictedRisks.rootCause: The project has materially diverged from the 16-week SOW milestone model, but no formal approved change request or contract amendment is evidenced in the provided sources.
triggerConditions: Deployment and hypercare continue against revised dates without documented amendment
Milestone invoicing is attempted against original schedule definitions
Stakeholders disagree on whether added PAT/regression effort is in-scope
Acceptance decisions are delayed due to baseline ambiguity

potentialImpact.schedule: Governance friction may delay approvals and final closure
potentialImpact.cost: Payment dispute or additional compensation discussions may emerge
potentialImpact.quality: Teams may rush closure activities to align to disputed milestone triggers
potentialImpact.customer: Trust and expectation management may deteriorate between client and vendor
potentialImpact.operations: Hypercare ownership and transition obligations may become unclear

supportingPatterns: Historical risk explicitly cited regression and extended PAT added outside original SOW
Historical mitigation effectiveness was low because operational replanning occurred without strong formal governance closure
Current project intelligence explicitly identifies no documented formal approval for extension

predictedRisks.estimatedResolutionTime: Short-Medium (1-2 weeks for agreement; longer if disputed)
mitigationPlan: Issue formal change-control package covering revised timeline, milestones, testing scope, and acceptance triggers
Reconcile payment milestones to actual lifecycle gates
Document what is in-scope defect resolution versus deferred enhancement work
Secure executive sponsor approval before deployment readiness reviews
recommendations: Do not wait until deployment to formalize the extension and milestone alignment
Create a single approved baseline for timeline, PAT/regression scope, and invoice triggers
Record acceptance criteria for revised gates in steering governance minutes
predictedRisks.reasoning: The extension from Sep 11 to Oct 30 is strongly evidenced in current project intelligence and uploaded documents, but formal approval is not documented. Historical evidence shows the same governance weakness already emerged in this delivery context and was only partially mitigated.
monitoringIndicators: Open disputes on in-scope vs enhancement items
Invoice trigger alignment to revised dates

projectIndicators: Original SOW end date Sept 11, 2026; current timeline extends through Oct 30, 2026
